course_description:
Integrative course concerned with ecosystems, communities & species at risk. Practical approaches to overcoming threatening processes, & underlying theory. Landscape ecology & regional ecosystems; spatial analysis; biological invasion and extinctions; in situ & ex situ methods. Interaction of science with social/legal context.

In BIOL3000 (Conservation), we will explore what can be done to repair the damage that people have done to the planet’s species, communities and natural ecosystems. Conservation is all about using science to help solve real world problems. Beginning with an understanding of natural patterns in biological diversity, we will chart human impacts on the natural world through overexploitation, habitat destruction, population declines, extinctions, invasions of exotic species and climate change. We will then look at tools to reverse these problems, including designing networks of nature reserves, economic incentives, habitat restoration, climate adaptation, and evidence-based conservation. Assessments are designed to stimulate application of intuition and knowledge to solve or explore conservation problems.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify conservation issues and the key ecological, social and political factors involved with them.
Learn to critically analyse a conservation issue and present that information in concise writing
Apply science to solve real conservation problems.
Evaluate arguments about conservation issues, expressing them verbally and in written form.
Contribute in a professional manner to a team to achieve successful outcomes

assessment_details.title: Prac assessment 2
assessment_details.task_description: The two practical sessions led by Prof Salit Kark and tutors will aim to help students discuss and better understand the process of set priorities for invasive and native species management and biodiversity conservation, using a case study of issues related to management of native and introduced alien species. You will develop your own conservation and management plan for native and invasive species in Queensland and describe this in a written assessment in teams. The Prac work and this assessment will be undertaken in small groups, enhancing your team work skills, which are key in both conservation and management in the real world. assessment_details.title: Prac assessment 3
assessment_details.task_description: The two practical sessions led by A/Prof Tatsuya Amano will focus on how we can systematically synthesise scientific evidence for conservaiton. You will learn how to use existing literature databases and search systems to conduct systematic literature searches and identify scientific evidence relevant to conservation in an unbiased and comprehensive manner. You will complete a short written assessment (less than 600 words) on developing, refining, and evaluating search strings for a systematic review, using the knowledge and approaches learned during the two sessions. Full instructions will be given in class. The prac work may be done in pairs or groups, but this assessment MUST be done individually.
